Create a TRANSPARENT pixel-art sprite sheet for the exact SAME small RPG villager shown in the first two reference images: young male grain loader, tousled charcoal-black hair, rust-red short-sleeved shirt, dark charcoal trousers, brown boots, a little brown belt pouch. Match the original low-resolution 24-by-36-pixel game sprite body and its mature/slender proportions, face and costume. The third reference is ONLY a pose/identity guide; don't use its huge chibi head. Draw complete new anatomically natural bodies, not pasted or stretched limbs. Crisp hard pixel clusters, NO antialiasing, no painterly texture, no labels, no ground, no background, NO BAG or cloth baked into the body. His empty cupped hands will later grip a separate 12-by-12-pixel sack in game. Shoulders-to-elbow and elbow-to-hand lengths stay consistent across all frames; fixed shoe size and head size. Stationary poses keep both soles on one baseline, knees bend under hips with torso hinging forward naturally.

EXACT sheet layout: 4 equal columns and 6 equal rows (24 isolated full-body sprites), generous transparent gutters, one character centered per cell, NO overlap. Each row is a timeline or set described below. All cells use the same scale. Hands belong in front of waist when carrying (about one-third of body height above feet).
Row 1, four front-facing lift stages: controlled bent-knee squat with straight back and both palms reaching low near shins; balanced half-squat grasp with both palms rising toward knees; nearly upright with elbows bent supporting empty sack space at lower waist; fully standing with both hands cupped at waist around empty sack space. Make legs realistically compress during squat, not feet anchored with knees jutting forward.
Row 2, four RIGHT-facing placement stages: upright holding empty sack space at waist with both hands; lean slightly and extend cupped hands forward a little; lower hands onto unseen cart edge; release and return hands near waist. Side-view face and torso must genuinely face RIGHT. Arms must NOT elongate to reach.
Row 3, four stationary work stages: front inspection glance down with hands relaxed near thighs; front shallow inspection stoop reaching low; front bend to pull a cloth forward (empty hands); front ease the cloth down and recover. No actual cloth or bag is visible.
Row 4, four detail poses: LEFT-facing glance toward coworker, hands still holding empty sack space; same left-facing look with slight head turn; RIGHT-facing tightening/checking rope with naturally bent elbows near waist; RIGHT-facing relaxed check pose with elbows closer to torso. No ropes/props baked in.
Row 5, four standing carry holds (feet shoulder-width, no walking): FRONT, BACK, LEFT, RIGHT respectively. In all four, BOTH hands support an empty sack area at waist, and elbows stay close to torso. In the back view his hands are in front of his torso and mostly occluded. In left/right views, the empty sack area is forward of the chest/waist.
Row 6, four front rest/effort poses: small shoulder roll and hands on hips; relax shoulders and exhale; controlled bent-knee shared lowering with hands at lower thigh height; slightly deeper shared lowering with hands near knee height. Keep feet planted, hips drop naturally, head and torso proportions unchanged.

This is a production animation sheet, not concept art. Every cell must have the same character with consistent natural proportions and a clean transparent background. Do not bake ANY grain sack, cart, ground shadow, floor or text into the body.

Create a TRANSPARENT production pixel-art sprite sheet of the SAME small male grain-loader as the attached reference: charcoal-black tousled hair, rust-red short-sleeved shirt, charcoal trousers, brown boots and belt pouch. Keep the low-resolution RPG game proportions and crisp pixel clusters, natural consistent arm/leg lengths and SAME body height in ALL frames. Full authored bodies, not pasted or stretched limbs. No antialiasing or painterly texture. No text, no background, no shadows, no ground, NO BAG/CART/PROPS baked into character. Both cupped hands support a separate invisible small sack at waist height; elbows close to torso, fingers just outside the empty sack area. A separate game prop will fill this space. Arms remain bent under load. BACK view hands and load are mostly occluded by his torso.

EXACT grid: FOUR equal columns and SIX equal rows =24 full-body sprites, clean transparent gutters. All frames same scale, feet on the same baseline within every cell. These are gentle walking cycles with short realistic steps under a load, no running or exaggerated extension. The head stays aligned with spine, no grotesque knee bend. Each walk row shows step-left/contact, passing, step-right/contact, passing.
Row1 four FRONT-facing loaded walk frames, looking toward viewer, sack held centered in front of waist. Hands cup empty sack space.
Row2 four BACK-facing loaded walk frames, looking AWAY from viewer, back of head/shirt visible, hands IN FRONT OF TORSO and therefore mostly hidden. Do not draw hands or sack over the character's back.
Row3 four LEFT-facing side-profile loaded walk frames. ALL noses point toward the LEFT edge of the sheet. Both arms support the empty sack area FORWARD on the LEFT side of torso. Do NOT face these right. This entire row travels LEFT.
Row4 four RIGHT-facing side-profile loaded walk frames. ALL noses point toward RIGHT edge of sheet. Both arms support empty sack area FORWARD on RIGHT side of torso.
Row5 four RIGHT-facing stationary supported-push poses: a sack is already resting on an unseen cart at waist height in front of him; one palm presses its near/left edge and the other arm relaxes. Begin slight lean with bent elbow and palm just ahead of waist; push a short distance forward by extending elbow naturally; lean from hips only a little; finish with one palm slightly farther ahead while other hand remains relaxed.
